C-HOMEBREW-RELEASE-TAP.Summary: Publish a Homebrew cask for trainings-logger into danielsavinoff/homebrew-tap on stable releases, document installation, validate, commit and push to the main application repository.

Goals.Goal: Connect the existing GoReleaser release pipeline to the user-created public homebrew-tap repository using HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN.
Make macOS installation and upgrades available through Homebrew and update README accordingly.

Constraints.Constraint: Use repository main, Casks directory and cask/binary name trainings-logger. Use repository-scoped HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN only for tap publication; retain GITHUB_TOKEN for application releases.
Read DROPBOX_APP_KEY from repository secrets, matching the user configuration already established; fail early for either missing app key or tap token without printing values.
Preserve current six-target builds, linker app-key injection, executable-plus-LICENSE archives and README exclusion. Stable releases update the tap; prereleases skip tap updates.

Handle the current unsigned macOS binary with the documented GoReleaser post-install hook, removing only the quarantine attribute from the staged trainings-logger binary, without changing system-wide security settings.
Do not run the real app, change user data, retrieve secret values, publish an actual release or push a tag. Validate with placeholder credentials and temporary snapshot artifacts.

Preserve unrelated user changes. The user explicitly authorized a commit and push to the application repository when done. Execute sequentially and archive completed GRACE work under existing authorization.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No new source behavior, Windows/Linux package managers, Apple signing credentials, native installers, automatic self-updates or live tap writes outside the release workflow.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: GoReleaser generates a cask with correct release URLs, checksums, Intel/Apple Silicon assets, trainings-logger binary artifact, scoped install hook, and danielsavinoff/homebrew-tap destination.
The GitHub workflow passes secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN and secrets.DROPBOX_APP_KEY, checking both before GoReleaser. No token is printed or embedded into the cask/application.
README leads with the macOS Homebrew install/run/upgrade commands and retains concise Linux/Windows download instructions.

Temporary GoReleaser snapshots and cask parsing validate packaging without publication. Build/vet/format and final GRACE checks pass. Archive, create a focused commit and push it to origin/main without creating a release tag.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user confirms the tap repository and HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN secret are ready. Public git inspection confirms main exists. The token value is available only to GitHub Actions and is not needed for local placeholder verification.
The first real cask publication occurs on the next stable v* tag after the committed workflow change. The user requested commit/push, not release/tag publication.
